events.description:
Auburn, Washington has been designated by the Veterans Day National Committee and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as a Regional Site for the 2026 celebration of Veterans Day.

The City of Auburn is proud to be a Vietnam War Commemorative Partner and considers it an honor and privilege to host this annual event. Auburn has hosted the Veterans Parade since 1965. The 2026 parade marks our 61st year! Over time, the parade has grown into one of the largest parades of its kind in the United States of America.

The purpose of Auburn’s Veterans Parade & Observance is to positively focus on honoring our country’s veterans and active military personnel. Recognition is focused on congressionally recognized Veteran Service Organizations and their auxiliaries, the military and military reserve, National Guard, and ROTC. The goal of Auburn’s Veterans Parade & Observance is to honor to our country’s veterans and to their military missions of defending freedom around the world.

The 61st annual Veterans Parade will be held in Auburn on Saturday, November 7, 2026 starting at 11:00 AM. The parade typically boasts over 120 units and nearly 4,000 parade participants, including more than 10 marching bands, numerous military vehicles, veterans’ units, honor guards and more.

The parade route travels west along Main Street from E Street to A Street NW/SW. The day-long activities run from 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

events.summary: Diwali: Lights of India will take place November 7, 2026 in the Armory Food & Event Hall.
events.description:
Diwali: Lights of India will take place November 7, 2026 in the Armory Food & Event Hall. The festival is part of the Seattle Center Festál series. It is free and open to the public.

Seattle Center Festál presents Diwali: Lights of India in partnership with Northwest Share. This year’s festival features music, dance, visual art, martial arts, a cooking demonstration and more.

HISTORY

Diwali (Festival of Lights) is a major cultural celebration observed throughout India every fall. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. Light is a metaphor for knowledge and consciousness. During Diwali in India, houses and business locations are brightly illuminated with lamps, diyas (oil lamps), and candles. Lakshmi, the Goddess of Wealth, is worshiped for prosperity. Diwali is celebrated with families and friends, wearing new clothes, partaking in family feasts, enjoying delicious sweets, sharing gifts and most importantly, setting off firecrackers!

The American Romanian Cultural Society is proud to announce the complete program for the 13th Romanian Film Festival Seattle, themed “Beyond Borders.” The festival will take place at SIFF Cinema Uptown and will feature in-person events and special international guests.

This year’s theme looks at the lines that shape our world: those carried in memory, left by hardship, and lightened by the laughter of everyday life. Through a mix of comedies and dramas, the selected films show how visible and invisible boundaries can become spaces of change.

Opening Night
The festival opens with “3 Days in September,” directed by Tudor Giurgiu. In this dark comedy, a bride’s wedding is disrupted when her fiancé’s pregnant mistress arrives, setting off a chaotic, real-time journey through a seaside resort that ends in unexpected freedom. Actress Andrea Vasile will attend the screening as a special guest, and an Opening Night Gala will follow immediately after the film.

Closing Night
The festival closes with “The Wall,” directed by Ion Borș and Ruslan Moroșan. This comedy follows a quarrel between two neighbors that pulls an entire quiet Moldovan village into escalating, comic feuds driven by pride, old grudges, and half-truths. Writer and producer Artur Erhan will join the screening as a special guest.

events.placeLines:

events.summary: Every year, the greater Gig Harbor community celebrates the return of salmon to our local waters.
events.description:
Every year, the greater Gig Harbor community celebrates the return of salmon to our local waters. The Donkey Creek Chum Festival serves to remind us that the quality of our water, and the habitat it supports, connects us all.

Participants will start their walk at Austin Park along Harborview Drive where they will receive a Salmon Passport. They will visit booths with activities and information for kids and adults along the trail through txʷaalqəł Estuary, behind the Harbor History Museum, and ending in Donkey Creek Park. Completed passports should be turned in to the front desk at the Harbor History Museum by 2pm on the day of the event to be entered into a drawing for a salmon-themed prize.

The goal of our salmon festival is to bring people together to promote sustainability, sound environmental stewardship, preservation of our maritime history and culture, responsible recreation, habitat preservation, and shoreline restoration — one salmon at a time. Join us on November 15th as we recognize new ways to improve and protect our waterways!

This event is free and open to people of all ages and abilities. The trail is less than 0.25 in length on a gravel packed pathway. Free public parking is available at the Museum, along Harborview Drive and Austin Street.

Please join us after Tot Shabbat for a Multi-Sensory Immersive Space for Discovery

The Schwartz ECS Light Lab opens its exhibit doors this month and will provide a space where young students will engage in a rich, multi-sensory environment for discovery, experimentation and collaboration. Within this immersive space, children will explore scientific concepts such as reflection, refraction, transparency, shadows and cause-and-effect relationships as they observe how light interacts with different materials, surfaces and even their own bodies.

Through creative and artistic expression, children will experiment with color mixing, projected light and shadow play to create both abstract and representational artwork, using light as a tool for storytelling and visual communication. These explorations naturally connect to Hanukkah, as children investigate the properties and symbolism of light through both scientific inquiry and cultural meaning.

The Light Lab also supports foundational literacy and mathematical development as children build vocabulary related to light. Such as glow, prism, spectrum and shadow, all while engaging with literacy-rich materials through a light-based lens. The Schwartz ECS Light Lab opens its exhibit doors this month and will provide a space where young students will engage in a rich, multi-sensory environment for discovery, experimentation and collaboration. Within this immersive space, children will explore scientific concepts such as reflection, refraction, transparency, shadows and cause-and-effect relationships as they observe how light interacts with different materials, surfaces and even their own bodies.

Through creative and artistic expression, children will experiment with color mixing, projected light and shadow play to create both abstract and representational artwork, using light as a tool for storytelling and visual communication. These explorations naturally connect to Hanukkah, as children investigate the properties and symbolism of light through both scientific inquiry and cultural meaning.

fairs and food festivals often charge admission and are still wanted. Anything that is one of the
